title: Kestrel Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the Nov 16th production incident where inference latency spiked for Kestrel's control-systems pipeline. We reviewed root cause analysis (KV cache eviction + autoscaler edge case), mitigation deployed (hotfix + temporary routing to dedicated capacity), monitoring improvements, and agreed next steps: share full postmortem doc, provide kernel-level logs, validate fix in staging, and schedule a verification call next week.
topics: Root cause: KV cache eviction + autoscaler race
Customer concerns: data retention, VPC, SLA implications

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20T15:00:00Z | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Miranda Lee (Redwood AE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Hannah Cole (Redwood CSM), Aisha Rahman (CTO, Kestrel), Diego Morales (Head of Infra, Kestrel), Priya Nair (SRE, Kestrel), Liam Chen (Product, Kestrel)

Auto-generated Summary: (brief) follow-up on incident on 2026-11-16 impacting control-systems inference latency. Hotfix applied, routing to dedicated capacity, verifying longer-term fixes.

00:00 - 00:18 Miranda: hey everyone, thanks for making time today, we'll keep this tight, jamal's got the technical recap, i'll cover customer-facing items and next steps
00:19 - 00:46 Jamal: yeah, hi, hi all. quick recap - on the 16th we saw a latency spike across their control pipeline, tail-latency went from ~120ms to 2.1s for a period of about 14 minutes. requests queue'd up, autoscaler didn't kick the expected extra nodes fast enough, and we saw repeated KV cache misses which amplified token compute.
00:47 - 01:10 Aisha: to be clear, this affected only the control path model, not telemetry ingestion, correct? we had a few fails in the loop that caused some timeouts and retries.
01:11 - 01:35 Jamal: correct, telemetry unaffected. root cause we believe is twofold: an edge-case in our autoscaler plus simultaneous cache eviction during a GC window - the cache eviction caused cold-starts for KV lookups, and autoscaler decision logic misread transient CPU metrics and didn't trigger scale soon enough.
01:36 - 02:02 Diego: i guess my question is why did the fallback routing not trigger? we had route policy to fallback to dedicated capacity when latency > 500ms for 30s, but that didn't seem to flip.
02:03 - 02:25 Miranda: good question - quick answer is the routing policy threshold used a smoothed metric which underweighted the short 14-minute spike and because the signal dipped below threshold briefly the policy never fully flipped. that's on us to make clearer in runbooks.
02:26 - 03:05 Priya: also noticed in our logs a small number of 5xxs around the time - were those from the inference runtime or from our client retries? some traces show connection resets.
03:06 - 03:30 Jamal: a mix. some were client-side timeouts retried, others were internal OOMs on a subset of nodes where the quantized kernel briefly exceeded memory due to concurrent cold KV fills. noisy but rare.
03:31 - 04:00 Liam: can we get an artifact - like a timeline trace with request IDs - for our postmortem. ops team wants to stitch it into our incident timeline.
04:01 - 04:20 Jamal: yes, we've started collecting traces, will drop a secured S3 link. Miranda will coordinate access.
04:21 - 04:55 Miranda: quick note on mitigation: within 20 minutes of detection we rolled a hotfix that changed eviction policy and forced KV cache warm-up on new nodes, and we temporarily routed the control path to dedicated capacity pool for Kestrel while the hotfix propagated. that brought tail-latency back to baseline within ~8 minutes.
04:56 - 05:20 Aisha: appreciate that. two questions: 1) was the hotfix a code change or config? 2) is this something that could reoccur during heavy traffic?
05:21 - 05:50 Jamal: hotfix was a config + small runtime patch to delay aggressive eviction during node initialization; the long-term fix will involve a change to kernel scheduling and autoscaler hysteresis. we believe recurrence risk is low after patch, but we need to validate across their traffic patterns.
05:51 - 06:30 Diego: okay, what about SLA credit and what hit our customers? we had two downstream control loops that retried, one failure briefly affected simulation runs. nothing catastrophic but operationally annoying.
06:31 - 06:55 Hannah: from support we'll open a formal credit request for the downtime window, and we'll include a timeline and mitigation notes in the ticket. we'll propose a proportional credit consistent with Redwood's policy - i'll follow up with the support ticket id.
06:56 - 07:20 Priya: we also want to understand data retention and logs - do you have packet-level traces or kernel metrics that show eviction counts? our security team will need to review what was shared.
07:21 - 08:00 Jamal: yes, we have eviction counters, per-node GC traces, and kernel scheduling logs. we'll sanitize any PII and provide secure access.
08:01 - 09:00 Aisha: from the CTO lens, two big asks: 1) ensure this doesn't impact safety-critical loops again, 2) give us a visible monitoring dashboard + alerting we control or can read. ideally RBAC to limit who can change routing.
09:01 - 10:15 Miranda: absolutely. short-term: we'll add a dedicated dashboard tile for eviction rate and tail-latency with an alert at 500ms sustained for 60s, and we'll propose an RBAC model for route changes. long-term: autoscaler logic changes and a canary policy so routing flips happen fast and are observable.
10:16 - 12:00 Diego: can you explain the autoscaler race? i want to make sure our infra team understands the sequence - we had a transient bump in CPU and memory but it looks like the scaler considered it noise.
12:01 - 14:10 Jamal: sure - the autoscaler uses a smoothed CPU metric with a 45s window to avoid flapping. in this case, concurrent cache cold fills spiked CPU for short bursts but the smoothing damped the alarm. the patch we're proposing will: (1) add a KV-eviction signal as a separate input to scaling decisions, and (2) reduce the smoothing window for certain policy classes for safety-critical routes.
14:11 - 15:00 Priya: will that change increase flapping risk? we have seen aggressive scaling cause instability on our side with ephemeral nodes.
15:01 - 16:20 Jamal: valid concern - we'll add hysteresis and a cooldown for scale down, so we adjust only upwards quickly but scale down conservatively. we'll also provide a simulation tool to test your traffic shape against the new policy before rollout.
16:21 - 20:00 Liam: related question: can we pin a model variant or quantization level for the control route to reduce runtime variance?
20:01 - 22:10 Jamal: yes, pinning is supported. we recommended a slightly higher-precision quantization for critical loops to avoid kernel OOMs; cost delta is modest versus risk. we can provide a cost/latency tradeoff table.
22:11 - 24:40 Aisha: we need that table and an estimate for monthly cost delta if we pin to dedicated capacity with a higher precision variant - also include recommended batching and prefix caching config.
24:41 - 26:10 Miranda: we'll include a short appendix in the postmortem with cost estimates and recommended config (batching, cache TTLs, reserved capacity sizes).
26:11 - 30:00 Diego: any security implications of routing to dedicated pool? we run in our VPC with private deployment, is there extra egress or logging concerns?
30:01 - 31:20 Hannah: Routing to a dedicated pool for Kestrel in Redwood Dedicated is within your VPC boundary; no extra egress beyond the nodes. we'll confirm logging retention and KMS used for those nodes.
31:21 - 34:00 Priya: ok, next - testing plan. we want a list of tests we should run in staging to validate. load shape, cold-start, GC pressure, and failover.
34:01 - 36:30 Jamal: we'll provide a test harness script that replays a representative workload, plus a stress tool to force eviction and cold KV fills. we'll put that in the repo and coordinate a joint test window.
36:31 - 38:00 Aisha: timeline - when can we expect the permanent fixes?
38:01 - 39:40 Miranda: short-term hotfixs already deployed; permanent autoscaler + kernel changes target next sprint - we expect a patch in ~2 weeks and validation within 3 weeks (so roughly by 2026-12-11), we'll confirm exact dates in the postmortem.
39:41 - 41:00 Diego: fine. for our ops runbook, please include a playbook for detection -> temporary routing -> rollback.
41:01 - 42:20 Jamal: yes, playbook included - we will embed run commands, metrics to check, and who to call (SE oncall).
42:21 - 45:00 Miranda: recap / next steps: we'll send the full postmortem and patch diffs, jamal will upload traces, hannah will handle support/credits, and we'll schedule a 30-min verification call for next week. any other points?
45:01 - 46:10 Priya: please make sure the S3 link has least-privileged access and expires.
46:11 - 47:20 Jamal: will do, signed URLs with 7-day expiry.
47:21 - 48:00 Miranda: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invite. bye.
